docs.title: GridForge
docs.text:
GridForge is a compact Python toolkit for preparing standard PYPOWER/MATPOWER cases for custom power-system studies.

It provides named pandas tables and a small set of domain operations:

  • load and round-trip standard cases;
  • register custom component tables for Case copies and Excel exports;
  • build bus-to-device connection matrices from Case tables or external DataFrames;
  • build DC and AC network matrices, including PTDF and bus admittance;
  • save and load all Case tables using a multi-sheet GridForge Excel workbook.

GridForge leaves general table editing to pandas and numerical optimization to the user's preferred modeling package.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Install the package with:

python -m pip install powergridforge

Excel save/load is included in the normal installation.

For development setup, see the repository README.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import gridforge as gf
import pandas as pd

case = gf.load_case("case14")
bus = case["bus"]

# Randomly choose two bus IDs with positive PD.
solar_bus_ids = bus.loc[bus["PD"] > 0, "BUS_IDX"].sample(
    n=2, random_state=7
)

# Create a solar table with pandas.
solar = pd.DataFrame(
    {"BUS_IDX": solar_bus_ids.to_numpy(), "PG": [20.0, 30.0]}
)
case.add_component("solar", solar)
connection = case.connection_matrix("solar")  # Bus-to-solar location matrix.

# Solar is not automatically included in the DC/AC network equations.
dc = case.dc_model()
ac = case.ac_model()
print(connection.shape)
print(dc.ptdf.shape)
print(ac.Ybus.shape)

# Excel round-trip; choose a new path or pass overwrite=True on reruns.
case.to_excel("scenario.xlsx")  # Raises if the file already exists.
restored = gf.load_excel("scenario.xlsx")

docs.title: AC Network Model
docs.text:
case.ac_model() constructs an AC network snapshot. It does not solve a power flow or include device generation and demand. No slack bus or connected network is required merely to build admittance matrices.

import numpy as np
import gridforge as gf

case = gf.load_case("case14")
ac = case.ac_model()

bus = case["bus"]
V = bus["VM"].to_numpy() * np.exp(1j * np.deg2rad(bus["VA"].to_numpy()))
Sbus_pu = V * np.conj(ac.Ybus @ V)
Sf_pu = (ac.Cf @ V) * np.conj(ac.Yf @ V)
St_pu = (ac.Ct @ V) * np.conj(ac.Yt @ V)

V is built from the current bus.VM and bus.VA values, which are not necessarily a power-flow solution. The formulas calculate network injections and branch-end flows at that voltage. Multiply complex power by case.base_mva to obtain MVA.

The returned ACModel contains:

Field Shape Meaning bus_ids nbus IDs Real BUS_IDX values in current bus-table row order branch_buses nbranch pairs Real from/to IDs in current branch-table row order Cf, Ct nbranch × nbus Physical from/to bus connection matrices Ybus nbus × nbus Complex bus admittance: Ibus = Ybus @ V Yf, Yt nbranch × nbus Complex branch-end admittances: If = Yf @ V, It = Yt @ V base_mva scalar Power base used to scale GS and BS

The matrices are SciPy CSR sparse matrices. Rows and columns follow current DataFrame row order, not DataFrame index labels or numeric bus-ID order. The model is an uncached snapshot; rebuild it after editing bus, branch, or base_mva.

For each online branch, GridForge uses series impedance BR_R + j*BR_X, half of the total BR_B charging at each end, and a complex tap defined by TAP and SHIFT (degrees). TAP=0 means a unit ratio. Bus shunts enter Ybus as (GS + j*BS) / base_mva; do not count these shunts again as constant-power load. These conventions match MATPOWER makeYbus.

An offline branch keeps its row and physical endpoints in Cf/Ct, but its Yf and Yt rows are zero and it contributes nothing to Ybus.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: General selection, row creation, and value edits use pandas on case["table_name"].

docs.title: Loaders and Case operations
docs.text:
Call Input Result / effect gf.load_case(source) Built-in PYPOWER name, local .py, local MATPOWER .m, or PYPOWER mapping Independent Case containing only standard core tables. Unknown top-level fields are ignored. gf.load_excel(path) .xlsx created in the current GridForge workbook format Independent Case with all table sheets, added columns, metadata, and recorded standard export schema. case["name"] Exact table name The Case's mutable pandas DataFrame; edits affect later operations and exports. case.table_names() — List of available names in stored order. case.tables — Read-only mapping of names to mutable DataFrames. case.copy() — Independent copy of tables and metadata. case.add_component(name, dataframe) New name and DataFrame Registers a copy; returns None. case.connection_matrix(component) Table name or external DataFrame with BUS_IDX New dense NumPy (nbus, ndevice) location matrix. case.dc_model(slack_bus=None) Optional real BUS_IDX reference New DCModel snapshot; dense NumPy matrices and p.u. flow terms. case.ac_model() — New ACModel snapshot; SciPy CSR admittance and connection matrices. case.to_pypower() — Independent standard PYPOWER dictionary; custom tables and columns omitted. case.to_python(path, overwrite=False) .py path Saves a standalone NumPy-only PYPOWER case function and returns the path. Preserves standard values and loaded result columns; refuses an existing file unless overwrite=True. case.to_excel(path, overwrite=False) .xlsx path Saves all Case tables and returns the path. Refuses an existing file unless overwrite=True.

Case also supports "solar" in case, iteration over table names, and len(case) as the number of tables. base_mva, version, and metadata are Case attributes; metadata does not enter PYPOWER export. Matrix results are independent snapshots, not live views of the Case.

For the exact import/export boundaries—including how added columns and custom tables are retained—see Cases and tables. The worked tutorial shows these calls together in a study.

docs.title: Matrix axes and units
docs.text:
Object Row axis Column axis Notes connection_matrix() Current bus row order Current component row order Dense; each device column has exactly one 1, regardless of STATUS. dc.Bf Current branch row order Current bus row order Maps angles (rad) to branch flows (p.u.). dc.ptdf Current branch row order Current bus row order Dimensionless sensitivity; absolute flows also need ptdf_flow_offset. dc.Bbus Current bus row order Current bus row order Maps angles (rad) to bus injections (p.u.). ac.Ybus Current bus row order Current bus row order Maps bus voltages to bus currents; complex CSR admittance. ac.Yf, ac.Yt Current branch row order Current bus row order Map bus voltages to branch-end currents; complex CSR admittance. ac.Cf, ac.Ct Current branch row order Current bus row order Map bus voltages to branch-end voltages; 0/1 CSR connections.

Align external bus vectors to dc.bus_ids or ac.bus_ids before matrix multiplication; neither model sorts by bus ID.

Divide MW by case.base_mva before applying p.u. DC equations; multiply complex p.u. power by that base to obtain MVA.

See Connection matrices, the DC model, and the AC network model for equations and limits.

docs.title: Public errors
docs.text: Error Typical cause gf.CaseLoadError Unsupported or malformed PYPOWER/MATPOWER input or GridForge workbook. gf.CaseValidationError Edited standard Case cannot be exported to a dictionary/Python file, or a value cannot be written safely to Excel. gf.ComponentValidationError Invalid component registration or invalid bus-to-device mapping. gf.DCNetworkError Invalid/disconnected DC network, ambiguous slack, or unreliable reduced solve. gf.ACNetworkError Invalid AC network parameters or bus references.

docs.title: Cases and Tables
docs.text: A Case holds editable pandas tables. Load a standard PYPOWER/MATPOWER case, edit or add tables, then use to_pypower() for the standard electrical model or to_excel()/load_excel() to retain the complete GridForge Case.

docs.title: Loading a Case
docs.text:
load_case() accepts:

  • a built-in PYPOWER case name;
  • a local PYPOWER .py case;
  • a local MATPOWER .m case;
  • a PYPOWER dictionary, for example the result of case14().
import gridforge as gf

case = gf.load_case("case14")
copied = case.copy()  # Independent copy; load_case(case) is not supported.

from pypower.api import case14
case = gf.load_case(case14())  # A PYPOWER dictionary is accepted too.

For an end-to-end example using pandas edits and three custom device types, see the worked tutorial. For short signatures and return types, see the API reference.

docs.title: Standard input boundary
docs.text:
load_case() reads only version, baseMVA, bus, gen, branch, and optional gencost. Other top-level fields, including custom solar or battery data, are ignored. Supported matrix layouts are listed at the end of this page.

load_case() checks table structure, unique bus IDs, and the bus references in gen and branch. dc_model() and ac_model() check the electrical parameters they use; only dc_model() requires a connected online network.

docs.title: Named Tables
docs.text:
case[name] returns a mutable pandas DataFrame. Standard tables are bus, gen, branch, and optional gencost:

bus = case["bus"]
bus["PD"]
case["gen"]["PMAX"]
case["branch"]["F_BUS_IDX"]

GridForge gives these columns readable names such as BUS_IDX, PD, PMAX, F_BUS_IDX, and STATUS. Column order and meanings follow the MATPOWER case format, but some GridForge names differ: BUS_IDX replaces BUS_I or GEN_BUS, F_BUS_IDX replaces F_BUS, and STATUS replaces GEN_STATUS or BR_STATUS in the corresponding tables.

BUS_IDX contains the real case bus identifier; it is not the DataFrame index or row position. Non-contiguous and unsorted bus IDs are preserved.

Direct pandas edits are intentional:

case["bus"].loc[case["bus"]["BUS_IDX"] == 4, "PD"] = 60
branch = case["branch"]
line_1_2 = (branch["F_BUS_IDX"] == 1) & (branch["T_BUS_IDX"] == 2)
branch.loc[line_1_2, "STATUS"] = 0

docs.title: Adding a Component Table
docs.text:
Create device rows with pandas, then register the completed DataFrame:

import pandas as pd

solar = pd.DataFrame({"BUS_IDX": [2, 6], "PMAX": [50.0, 80.0]})
case.add_component("solar", solar)

# Registration copies the DataFrame; edit the stored table thereafter.
case["solar"].loc[0, "PMAX"] = 60

add_component() registers a copy and returns None. Use pandas to create or edit rows; registration does not update or replace an existing table.

BUS_IDX and device-specific parameters are not checked at registration. Tables without BUS_IDX can still be stored and exported, but connection_matrix() requires valid bus identifiers when building a map.

docs.title: PYPOWER Export
docs.text:
case["gen"]["TECHNOLOGY"] = "thermal"
ppc = case.to_pypower()
# TECHNOLOGY remains in the Case but is omitted from ppc["gen"].

to_pypower() uses the current values and row order of the standard tables. It exports their recorded PYPOWER columns in standard order, even if you reorder the DataFrame columns. This includes PF/OPF result columns present when loading. Added columns and custom component tables are omitted; gencost is omitted if absent.

docs.title: Python Case File Save and Load
docs.text:
Save the standard electrical model as an independent PYPOWER case:

case = gf.load_case("case14")
path = case.to_python("case_custom.py")

After saving to python file case_custom.py, you can load it using normal gridforge method.

restored = gf.load_case(path)

Similar to pypower style The filename stem becomes the function name. Existing files are protected unless overwrite=True.

The generated file requires only NumPy and works with normal Python imports and PYPOWER's file loader:

# From case_custom.py file import the function callsed case_custom
from case_custom import case_custom
ppc = case_custom()

# Alternatively
from pypower.loadcase import loadcase
same_case = loadcase("case_custom.py")

Each function call returns a fresh dictionary and independent arrays. Standard values, row order, bus IDs, empty matrix shapes and loaded PF/OPF result columns are preserved. Float literals retain full float64 precision; NaN and infinity are also preserved. Output follows gridforge's to_pypower(): added columns, custom tables and metadata are omitted, and absent gencost remains absent. Use Excel when those additional tables and metadata must be retained.

docs.title: Excel Save and Load
docs.text:
Save all Case tables, including registered components and added columns, then restore them with load_excel():

case.to_excel("scenario.xlsx")
restored = gf.load_excel("scenario.xlsx")
solar = restored["solar"]

Existing files are protected by default; use overwrite=True only when replacement is intended.

The workbook has one sheet per table and a case_info sheet for the power base, case version, metadata, and standard export schema. Table, row, and column order and real BUS_IDX values are retained. load_excel() accepts GridForge workbooks, while load_case() does not accept .xlsx files.

docs.title: Supported Standard Input Layouts
docs.text:
load_case() accepts these complete version-2 matrix layouts. Input arrays must retain the MATPOWER column order: GridForge cannot detect swapped columns when the width is still supported.

Table Supported column counts Meaning bus 13, 17 Standard input; OPF result columns gen 21, 25 Standard input; OPF result columns branch 13, 17, 21 Standard input; PF results; OPF results gencost Variable Parameters declared by each row's MODEL and NCOST

gencost, when present, has one active-power cost row per generator or twice as many rows for active and reactive costs. MODEL=1 uses NCOST power/cost pairs; MODEL=2 uses NCOST polynomial coefficients.

docs.title: Common PYPOWER case:
docs.text:
Name Description case4gs 4-bus, 2-generator case from Grainger & Stevenson case6ww 6-bus, 3-generator case from Wood & Wollenberg case9 9-bus, 3-generator case case9Q 9-bus case with reactive generation costs case14 IEEE 14-bus test case case24_ieee_rts IEEE Reliability Test System case30 30-bus, 6-generator case case30Q 30-bus case with reactive generation costs case30pwl 30-bus case with piecewise linear generator costs case39 39-bus New England system case57 IEEE 57-bus test case case118 IEEE 118-bus test case case300 IEEE 300-bus test case

Availability follows the installed PYPOWER version. See the PYPOWER source for the complete list.

docs.title: Connection Matrices
docs.text: case.connection_matrix(component) maps each component row to the bus named by its BUS_IDX. The result is a dense NumPy array describing location only. Pass a Case table name or an external pandas DataFrame with a BUS_IDX column. Passing a DataFrame directly does not register it in the Case.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
import gridforge as gf

case = gf.load_case("case14")
solar = pd.DataFrame(
    {"BUS_IDX": [2, 6], "PG": [20.0, 30.0], "STATUS": [1, 0]}
)
case.add_component("solar", solar)
C_solar = case.connection_matrix("solar")  # Shape: (14 buses, 2 solar rows)

Matrix rows follow the current bus-table row order; columns follow the current component-table row order. Pandas index labels do not determine these positions. Each component column has one 1 at its bus, even if multiple components share that bus.

For a separate three-bus example, if the bus order is [101, 205, 123] and two solar rows have BUS_IDX values [123, 101], the matrix is:

            solar row 0  solar row 1
bus 101          0            1
bus 205          0            0
bus 123          1            0

STATUS=0 does not remove or zero a connection column. Apply status and power values yourself when calculating bus injections:

solar_table = case["solar"]
solar_by_bus_mw = C_solar @ (
    solar_table["PG"] * solar_table["STATUS"]
).to_numpy()

GridForge does not infer power signs, convert MW to p.u., or balance injections. BUS_IDX values must be integer-valued and refer to existing buses. Rebuild the matrix after editing or reordering either table. See the worked tutorial for aggregation with other devices and demand.

docs.title: Third-Party Software
docs.text:
GridForge depends on third-party Python packages, including PYPOWER, pandas, NumPy, and SciPy. Those projects remain under their own licenses.

GridForge can load PYPOWER-style and MATPOWER-style case files. External case files and datasets remain under the licenses and terms provided by their authors or distributors.

Users are responsible for complying with the licenses of case files and other data they load, modify, or redistribute through GridForge.

docs.title: DC Model
docs.text:
case.dc_model() builds DC network matrices and a PTDF snapshot. It does not solve a power flow or dispatch generators.

import gridforge as gf

case = gf.load_case("case14")
dc = case.dc_model()  # Unique BUS_TYPE=3 bus is the default slack.

For case14, case.dc_model(slack_bus=2) selects bus ID 2 instead. The argument is a real BUS_IDX, not a DataFrame row position. An explicit slack can be any active bus; it need not have BUS_TYPE=3.

docs.title: Calculate branch flows
docs.text:
Supply bus_injection_pu yourself: a balanced array of net injections in p.u., ordered as dc.bus_ids. Injection is positive; withdrawal is negative. The worked tutorial shows how to construct and balance this array from generators, demand, GS, and custom devices.

branch_flow_pu = dc.ptdf @ bus_injection_pu + dc.ptdf_flow_offset

Flow is positive from F_BUS_IDX to T_BUS_IDX. The offset is required for absolute flows with phase-shifting transformers: it is not simply branch_shift_flow, because the network also responds to phase-shift bus injections. See my blog.

docs.title: Returned fields
docs.text:
Symbol GridForge field Shape Meaning / units — bus_ids nbus IDs Real BUS_IDX values in current bus-table order — branch_buses nbranch pairs Real endpoint IDs in current branch-table order — slack_bus, base_mva scalar Chosen real BUS_IDX and MVA power base A incidence nbranch × nbus Physical incidence: +1 at from bus, −1 at to bus B_f Bf nbranch × nbus Maps bus angles in radians to branch flows in p.u. B_bus Bbus nbus × nbus Maps bus angles in radians to bus injections in p.u. H ptdf nbranch × nbus Dimensionless flow sensitivities; slack column is zero p_f^(shift) branch_shift_flow nbranch Direct phase-shift branch-flow term, p.u. p_bus^(shift) bus_shift_injection nbus Phase-shift bus-injection term, p.u. p_f^(offset) ptdf_flow_offset nbranch Final fixed branch-flow term in the PTDF equation, p.u.

For an angle vector theta in radians:

bus_injection_pu = dc.Bbus @ theta + dc.bus_shift_injection
branch_flow_pu = dc.Bf @ theta + dc.branch_shift_flow

The PTDF formula above gives the same branch flows for balanced injections. For online branches, TAP=0 means a unit ratio, and SHIFT=0 means no phase shift. These settings leave the branch in service; set branch.STATUS=0 to take it out of service. SHIFT is specified in degrees. The equations and signs follow the MATPOWER makeBdc convention.

docs.title: Ordering, outages and errors
docs.text:
• Matrix axes follow current bus and branch row order, not pandas index labels or sorted bus IDs. GridForge does not renumber buses or drop branches.
  • An offline branch retains its row and physical endpoints in incidence, but its flow-related row and phase-shift terms are zero. Its bus references must still be valid.
  • The online network must be connected and have one slack bus. If BUS_TYPE=3 is missing or non-unique, specify slack_bus. Islands, invalid online parameters, or a singular network raise DCNetworkError.

DCModel contains dense NumPy arrays. Rebuild it after editing bus/branch data or base_mva. Editing its arrays does not modify the Case.

docs.title: Worked Tutorial: Edit a Case and Add Devices
docs.text: This example modifies case14, records solar generation, battery discharge, and data-centre demand in separate tables, then calculates DC branch flows. It illustrates the boundary between pandas edits and GridForge's network operations.

docs.title: 1. Load and edit the standard tables
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
import gridforge as gf

original = gf.load_case("case14")  # Load PYPOWER's built-in case14.
case = original.copy()             # Keep the reference Case unchanged.

bus = case["bus"]
gen = case["gen"]

# BUS_IDX is the physical bus number, not a pandas index label.
bus.loc[bus["BUS_IDX"] == 4, "PD"] = 60.0  # MW
gen.loc[gen["BUS_IDX"] == 2, "PG"] = 50.0  # MW; used below as generation

The returned DataFrames are mutable. A pandas edit through case["bus"] changes this Case and is reflected in later exports. It does not change original or any matrix snapshot built earlier.

docs.title: 2. Register custom component tables
docs.text:
solar = pd.DataFrame({"BUS_IDX": [2], "P_MW": [20.0], "STATUS": [1]})
battery = pd.DataFrame({"BUS_IDX": [6], "P_MW": [5.0], "STATUS": [1]})
data_center = pd.DataFrame({"BUS_IDX": [9], "P_MW": [15.0], "STATUS": [1]})

case.add_component("solar", solar)
case.add_component("battery", battery)
case.add_component("data_center", data_center)

add_component() copies each DataFrame into the Case. GridForge does not assign an electrical meaning to P_MW or STATUS: this example treats solar and battery discharge as injections, and data-centre power as demand. Edit the registered tables through case["solar"], etc.

docs.title: 3. Map devices to buses and calculate injections
docs.text:
def active_bus_power_mw(table_name):
    table = case[table_name]
    device_mw = (table["P_MW"] * table["STATUS"]).to_numpy()
    return case.connection_matrix(table_name) @ device_mw

solar_by_bus_mw = active_bus_power_mw("solar")
battery_by_bus_mw = active_bus_power_mw("battery")
center_by_bus_mw = active_bus_power_mw("data_center")

gen_by_bus_mw = case.connection_matrix("gen") @ (
    gen["PG"] * gen["STATUS"]
).to_numpy()

# All vectors now follow the current bus-table row order.
net_bus_mw = (
    gen_by_bus_mw
    + solar_by_bus_mw
    + battery_by_bus_mw
    - center_by_bus_mw
    - bus["PD"].to_numpy()
    - bus["GS"].to_numpy()
)
net_bus_pu = net_bus_mw / case.base_mva

The GS term is treated as a constant MW withdrawal under the DC approximation VM = 1. Change this policy if your study models shunts differently. connection_matrix() itself does not inspect STATUS, power columns, signs, or units; the explicit multiplication by STATUS above does that work.

docs.title: 4. Calculate DC branch flows
docs.text:
dc = case.dc_model()
assert tuple(bus["BUS_IDX"]) == dc.bus_ids

# Example balancing policy: the selected slack supplies any net mismatch.
# This does not check generator limits or perform dispatch.
balanced_bus_pu = net_bus_pu.copy()
slack_position = dc.bus_ids.index(dc.slack_bus)
balanced_bus_pu[slack_position] -= balanced_bus_pu.sum()

branch_flow_pu = dc.ptdf @ balanced_bus_pu + dc.ptdf_flow_offset
branch_flow_mw = branch_flow_pu * case.base_mva

for (from_bus, to_bus), flow_mw in zip(dc.branch_buses, branch_flow_mw):
    print(f"{from_bus} -> {to_bus}: {flow_mw:.2f} MW")

The PTDF offset matters when phase-shifting transformers are present. dc_model() leaves the Case unchanged; after a table edit, rebuild the snapshot and align vectors with its recorded axes. See the DC model for equations and network requirements. To build AC admittance matrices for a different study, use case.ac_model(); see the AC model.

docs.title: 5. Export the right representation
docs.text:
ppc = case.to_pypower()
assert "solar" not in ppc
assert "battery" not in ppc
assert "data_center" not in ppc

to_pypower() includes the edits to bus.PD and gen.PG, but omits the custom device tables. A PYPOWER calculation using ppc therefore does not include the solar, battery, or data-centre injections unless you translate them into standard tables.

The Excel format preserves the complete GridForge Case, including custom tables and added standard-table columns. This round trip uses a temporary file so the example can be run repeatedly:

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    workbook = Path(directory) / "scenario.xlsx"
    case.to_excel(workbook)
    restored = gf.load_excel(workbook)
    assert restored.table_names() == case.table_names()

For a lasting workbook, pass a path of your choice to to_excel(). See Cases and tables for overwrite behavior and the precise Excel/PYPOWER preservation rules.
